plan.summary: Prioritizing high-impact resource deployment to West Augustine, Lincolnville, and Uptown San Marco to maximize coverage across EMS, supply, and medical support metrics.

assignments.rationale: Clears roads to enable further response reach in West Augustine.
Provides necessary road access for Lincolnville.
Significant increase in EMS locations for West Augustine.
Expands EMS reach within Uptown San Marco.
Maximizes supply access locations in West Augustine.
Provides massive increase in medical support locations for Uptown San Marco.
Addresses water rescue needs in Lincolnville.
Addresses water rescue needs in West Augustine.
Establishes helicopter priority cluster in Uptown San Marco.

tradeoffs: Allocating debris crews to West Augustine and Lincolnville limits the ability to address other zones, but is necessary to unlock subsequent resource utility.
Focusing medical support in Uptown San Marco leaves other regions without dedicated medical support units.
plan.limitations_ack: Allocation is based on the greedy sequence provided; actual road network connectivity may vary from the sequential metric improvements.

base.label: Provisional response base (West 9th Street)
base.disclosure: Hypothetical response base chosen on a road that stays connected in every category. Real EMS/station locations are not in the dataset. The only OSM hospital node is a dead end that floods shut at Category 3+, so it cannot serve as a dispatch origin.

assumptions: Inventory is hypothetical (11 units); not real agency resources.
Debris obstructions are simulated (fixed seed, documented) and separate from NOAA flooding.
Clearing debris never reopens roads closed by modeled flooding.
EMS, supply and medical teams start from one provisional, hypothetical response base; real station locations are not modeled.
A 'location' is a road-network graph node, not a person or household; no population is modeled.

EMS coverage = locations within 1500 m of road travel from the team's point; supply access = locations within 1500 m of road travel TO the supply point. The radius is an assumption, not a response-time estimate.
Potential water rescue = flood-exposed locations within 500 m (straight line) of a road-reachable entry point; not a navigable route and not confirmed feasibility.
Potential helicopter rescue = one hypothetical priority cluster of at most 10 locations; no flight, landing or hoist feasibility is claimed and roads are unchanged.
Coverage categories (EMS, supply, medical support, water rescue, helicopter) are reported separately and never summed; hospital access is separate again.
result.notes: All numbers are computed by NetworkX over the provisional road graph; locations are graph nodes, not people.
